title: Greenhouse Jobs API Scraper
description: Fetch live job postings from Greenhouse using its public job-board API. Give it board tokens (anthropic) or Greenhouse careers URLs.

companies.title: Greenhouse board tokens or careers URLs
companies.description: One per line. A Greenhouse board token (anthropic) or a Greenhouse careers URL (https://job-boards.greenhouse.io/anthropic). The board token is the slug in your board URL. An entry for another ATS is refused with a free error row - use the multi-ATS Actor ats-jobs-scraper for those.

maxJobs.title: Max jobs (total)
maxJobs.description: Hard stop after this many charged job rows. Your main cost control. Companies not reached before the cap are never charged. Set 0 for no limit.

maxJobsPerCompany.title: Max jobs per company
maxJobsPerCompany.description: Stop after this many jobs from a single company. Useful when one enterprise board would eat the whole budget. Set 0 for no limit.

titleKeywords.title: Title must contain any of
titleKeywords.description: Case-insensitive substring match on the job title. Empty = no title filter. Filtering happens before billing, so filtered-out jobs are free.
titleKeywords.sectionDescription: All filters run locally on the fetched JSON. Jobs removed by a filter are never charged, and a company whose jobs were all filtered out costs you nothing at all.

excludeTitleKeywords.title: Title must NOT contain any of
excludeTitleKeywords.description: Case-insensitive substring match. Applied after titleKeywords. Example: intern, contract, principal.

locationKeywords.title: Location must contain any of
locationKeywords.description: Case-insensitive substring match on the raw location text and on the parsed city, region and country. A two-letter entry is matched exactly against the country code instead, so it cannot hit inside a word. Example: Berlin, Germany, EMEA.

remoteOnly.title: Remote jobs only
remoteOnly.description: Keep only jobs where remote could be positively determined (remote = true). Jobs with unknown remote status are dropped.

departments.title: Departments
departments.description: Case-insensitive substring match on the department or team name as reported by the ATS. Empty = all departments.

employmentTypes.title: Employment types
employmentTypes.description: Keep only these normalized employment types. Jobs whose type is unknown are kept unless you also enable strictEmploymentType.

strictEmploymentType.title: Only ATS-confirmed employment types
strictEmploymentType.description: Keep only jobs whose employment type came from the ATS itself, dropping both unknowns and types we guessed from the job title. Greenhouse boards almost never report a type, so this drops nearly every row - it is here for parity with the multi-ATS Actor, not because Greenhouse rewards it.

postedAfter.title: Posted after
postedAfter.description: Keep only jobs posted at or after this date, e.g. 2026-08-01 or '7 days'. Jobs with no posting date from the ATS are kept and flagged postedAtSource=null.

includeDescription.title: Include job description
includeDescription.description: On by default, at no extra cost: Greenhouse returns the ad body in the same response we already make, and you are billed per row either way. Makes items about 10x larger - turn it off for a slimmer dataset. The body stays the employer's copyrighted text. Contact details are stripped unless you turn redactContacts off. Executable markup (`<script>`, `<iframe>`, `on*=`, `javascript:`) is removed; the remaining HTML is the employer's own, so render it sandboxed.

descriptionFormat.title: Description format
descriptionFormat.description: Only used when includeDescription is on.

redactContacts.title: Redact contact details from descriptions
redactContacts.description: Strip contact details from the ad body: email addresses, phone numbers, LinkedIn/Xing/WhatsApp/Calendly/Telegram links and handles, and a person's name where the ad labels it as a contact (`Ansprechpartner:`, `Kontakt:`, `Contactpersoon:`, `Contact:`, `Hiring manager:`, `Recruiter:`). On by default — EU ads routinely close with a named contact. It does not catch a name in running prose: no label, no pattern. `descriptionRedacted` on each row says whether anything was removed.

outputProfile.title: Output profile
outputProfile.description: minimal = title, company, location, url, postedAt. compact = minimal plus remote, department, employmentType, salary. full = every field. Use minimal for AI agents to cut token cost.

includeCompanySummary.title: Add one summary row per company
includeCompanySummary.description: Adds a free company_summary row with total jobs found, jobs kept after filters, new jobs, duplicates dropped and top departments. Summary rows are never charged.

includeRawJson.title: Include raw ATS payload
includeRawJson.description: Attach the provider JSON for each job under raw, with contact-shaped fields and ad bodies removed. Large. Useful when you need a field we do not normalize.

dedupe.title: Deduplication
dedupe.description: id = drop repeats of the same ATS job id (always on). content = also merge same title + company + location + requisition id. May merge genuinely separate openings for the same role; leave off unless you see duplicates.

onlyNewJobs.title: Only jobs not seen in a previous run
onlyNewJobs.description: Compares against the ids stored under stateKey in your own named key-value store and outputs only new ones. The first run stores the baseline and outputs everything.

stateKey.title: State key
stateKey.description: Name of the key-value store that holds seen job ids for onlyNewJobs. Use a different key per monitoring task. Stored in your account, never sent anywhere.

stateRetentionDays.title: Forget job ids after N days
stateRetentionDays.description: Ids not seen for this many days are dropped from the state so it cannot grow forever. 0 keeps everything.

maxConcurrency.title: Max concurrent companies
maxConcurrency.description: Lower this if Greenhouse starts rate limiting. Per-host request rate is capped separately at 2 requests per second regardless of this value.

requestTimeoutSecs.title: Request timeout
requestTimeoutSecs.description: Per HTTP request timeout in seconds.

failOnAllErrors.title: Fail the run if every company failed
failOnAllErrors.description: When on, a run where no company returned any job exits with FAILED instead of SUCCEEDED. Useful in scheduled pipelines.
